From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenhealth.com>

Date: Fri, 27 Oct 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot traffic sample + quick questions on GPU sizing

Camila —

Thanks for the runbook link in the demo. We pulled a 7-day traffic extract and attached a small sample (lumen_traffic_sample.csv). Before the workshop next week, can you confirm the minimum info you need to produce a preliminary fleet sketch? At a minimum we can share: average tokens in prompt/response, typical concurrency, and percent streaming.

High-level context: this pilot is customer-facing search + summarization across clinical notes. Expected peak is during weekday mornings. We want a conservative sizing for a 3-month pilot with an option to scale.

A few quick answers from our side: average prompt ~45 tokens, average response ~220 tokens, session length ~2.5 minutes (most calls are single-turn), ~12% of requests use streaming.

I attached the sample. Let me know if you need anything else.

—Sanjay Rao
Director, Platform Engineering
LumenHealth

Attachment: lumen_traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 98 rows, anonymized timestamps)

Hi Sanjay —

Got the sample, thanks. I uploaded a Redwood sizing template and filled the first-pass fields (see attached redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx). To produce a meaningful preliminary fleet topology I typically need the following if you have them:
- Peak QPS or peak requests/minute (observed)
- Percent of requests that are multi-turn/sessioned vs single-turn
- P95/P99 response latency targets for the pilot (hard SLOs)
- KV-cache hit rate or whether requests are stateless (e.g., fresh prompt each call)
- Percent of requests that include tool/function calls or long context windows >2k tokens

From your sample numbers the average token count looks reasonable. Can you confirm peak QPS during weekday mornings and the P95 target? If you prefer, we can take the sample and run a quick token-bucket simulation and share a single-slide fleet suggestion before the kickoff.

I'll loop in Marissa for pricing guardrails and Karthik for topology assumptions.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (Excel, 1 tab)

Sanjay / Camila —

Quick notes from pricing/commit perspective: for a short 3-month pilot we usually recommend a small reserved pool (N GPUs) + burstable dedicated nodes to keep p99 below ~1.2s for standard generation models. Key knobs that materially change the number of GPUs: batching window (trade latency vs throughput), prefix caching (if you have repeat prompts), and percent streaming.

Two asks for sizing accuracy:
1) Can you share observed peak requests/minute and an example of a 1-hour peak slice? Even ballpark numbers help.
2) What is the acceptable p95/p99 for the pilot (SLA)? Is 1s p95 / 2s p99 acceptable or do you need sub-500ms p95?

If streaming is only 12% and KV cache hit rate is >40%, the GPU count drops significantly because we can avoid re-computing prefixes. If you want, we can run a fast simulation (Camila has the sample) and return a 1-slide estimate with GPU SKUs and expected monthly token cost.

—Marissa Cole
Head of Pre-Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the sample — I pulled a quick token histogram from Camila's sheet and sketched a conservative topology. Below are the fields that will change the GPU count materially and our current assumptions for a 3-month pilot: 

Key assumptions (conservative)
- Peak observed: 230 requests/minute (weekday morning peak)
- Average prompt: 45 tokens, average response: 220 tokens
- Single-turn requests: 88% (multi-turn 12%)
- Streaming percent: 12% (as noted)
- KV-cache hit rate assumed: 30% (we'll tune this in staging)
- Target latency: p95 <= 1.5s, p99 <= 3.0s
- Model: redwood-open-13b-quant (baseline) with quantized weights

Preliminary topology suggestion (high level)
- 4 x GPU nodes (reserved) sized at 80% occupancy for steady-state; 2 additional burst GPUs for peak windows.
- Autoscaler: minute-granularity scale-up with cold-start warm pools pre-warmed (helps with p99 spikes).
- Batching: 8–12 token batching window (configurable) to balance latency/throughput.
- Prefix caching: enable for repeated search prompts; with 30% hit we save ~20–30% compute on the fleet.

Notes / data asks
- If you can export a 1-hour peak slice with timestamps we will run a slotting sim and return a final GPU count.
- Provide the percent of calls that call external tools (e.g., retrieval, DB lookups) since tool calls add blocking time and impact concurrency math.

Next steps
- Camila and I will run the quick simulation and share a single-slide fleet sketch + cost ballpark by EOD today. If that looks good we can schedule a 45-minute sizing workshop with your infra and security on Thu.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the fast turnaround. We can provide a 1-hour peak slice (I'll export and drop in the Drive link) and confirm tool-call percentages (should be ~6% of requests). P95 target of 1.5s is fine for the pilot.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you include a line item for a canary plan (1–2 nodes) and estimated cost if we go from pilot to production (3x scale)?
- We also need a checklist of security artifacts for the procurement team (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, data retention policy). Can someone from your security team own that list?

If the simulation matches Karthik's sketch, let's lock a 45-min sizing workshop for Thu 14:00 PT. I'll cc contracts@lumenhealth.com once we have a pilot scoping doc.

—Sanjay
Director, Platform Engineering, LumenHealth
